tier_reason: The lzbench v1.8.1 README table has the lzmat 1.01 row (38 MB/s, 479 MB/s, 76,485,353, 36.09) next to zlib 1.2.11 -1 (119, 383) and -6 (35, 407), and the run is otherwise A-grade reproducible (public _lzbench/lzbench.cpp and compressors.cpp, Makefile flags at the v1.8.1 tag, clang 9.0.1, i7-8700K). It stays capped at C because the harness maintainer flags the measured decoder itself as buggy (v1.5 to 2026 master README: 'Decompression bugs', 'decompression error; returns 0'), following the uniwidth 'bug in hot path' precedent, even though lzbench's memcmp round-trip check passed on silesia.tar.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: clang 9.0.1; lzbench 1.8 run with -t16,16 -eall. Public Makefile at tag v1.8.1: OPT_FLAGS = -fomit-frame-pointer -fstrict-aliasing -ffast-math; lzmat_dec.c and lzmat_enc.c are built with -O2 -DNDEBUG under the Makefile's 'FIX for SEGFAULT on GCC 4.9+' rule, while zlib and most other codecs are built with -O3 -DNDEBUG.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 10 stars, 8 forks (single-commit git mirror of the 2008 LZMAT 1.01 release); bundled in lzbench since at least v1.5
corrections.caveats: Tier capped at C although the harness is reproducible: lzbench lists lzmat under 'security issues and/or no longer maintained' and has warned since v1.5 that it contains decompression bugs (decompression error, returns 0) and can segfault with GCC 4.9+ -O3. The 2026 master README still says 'Decompression bugs' and CompFuzz lists LZMAT as abandoned with issues found (2013-09-11, no details). The measured silesia.tar run itself round-tripped: lzbench 1.8 checks the decompressed length and memcmp after every decompression and would print ERROR instead of a speed, and the decoder compiled in is the bounds-checked LZMAT_SAVE path. Build asymmetry: lzmat was compiled at -O2 and zlib at -O3 in the same binary, which, if anything, favours zlib. The code measured is lzbench's patched copy (identical in v1.8.1 and master lz/lzmat), not the upstream repo as-is: nemequ/lzmat's lzmat_enc.c casts pointers to 32-bit MP_U32 in the output-bound check (line 426) and the output-size computation (line 463), which lzbench fixed for 64-bit builds, and lzbench also changed the MP_PTR typedef guard in lzmat.h, so copy from lzbench's lz/lzmat on LP64 targets. The lead is narrow (decompression only, about 1.2x over zlib) and the codec loses to LZO, LZ4 and Snappy in the same table. lzbench 2.4 no longer prints a lzmat row; v1.8.1 is the last tag that does (v1.5 and v1.7.3 gave 24 MB/s compress and 294/288 MB/s decompress against zlib -1 at 244/250 and -6 at 263/267 on an i5-4300U with gcc 6.x, the same about 1.1-1.2x decompression lead). The author's own claims on matcode.com returned 403 and the mirror seen in search results (autohotkey.com) is blocked, so no first-party numbers were read; the GitHub repo carries no README or benchmarks.

notes: Numbers and derived ratios check out exactly (479/383 = 1.25x, 479/407 = 1.18x, 119/38 = 3.1x slower compress), and license GPL-2.0-or-later (header: version 2 or any later version), last commit 2013-08-22 and 10 stars are confirmed. Main shortcomings to record: the harness maintainer flags the decoder as buggy, the decompression-only lead is about 1.2x over zlib and it loses to LZO, LZ4 and Snappy, and upstream nemequ/lzmat truncates pointers to 32 bits in the encoder on 64-bit targets (the measured copy is lzbench's fixed one). If the orchestrator treats the passing round-trip check as enough, the evidence otherwise meets tier A, consistent with the wave 9 lzbench retier-02.
